title: NEB Class 11 English — Writing — 2024
subject: english
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Write an essay on 'Importance of Reading Books' in about 250 words.
questions.solution:
Model essay:

Reading books is one of the most valuable habits one can develop. It broadens the mind, expands vocabulary, and deepens understanding of the world.

First, reading improves knowledge — history teaches from past mistakes, science reveals new discoveries. Second, it sharpens language: regular readers write and speak more clearly. Third, it relieves stress, offering escape from daily worries. Finally, stories build imagination, transporting us across worlds and time.

In conclusion, reading is not merely a hobby but a lifelong necessity that shapes character and intellect. Students should read daily.
questions.knowledgeNote: Essay frame: hook + thesis → body (topic sentence + explanation + example each) → conclusion. Examiners scan for this skeleton first.

questions.question: Write a letter to your friend describing your school excursion to Pokhara.
questions.solution:
Model informal letter:

Kathmandu, 15 April 2024

Dear Sita, I hope you are well. Our school excursion to Pokhara was unforgettable — the hillside drive, boating on Phewa Lake, the Peace Pagoda, and the Annapurna panorama from the top. The mountain museum and lakeside food made it perfect. Wish you had joined us! Regards to your family.

Your friend, Anita
questions.knowledgeNote: Informal letter: address + date + greeting + body (news, details, feelings) + close. Tone warm, contractions allowed.

questions.question: Write a news report on a road accident in your locality in about 200 words.
questions.solution:
Model structure:

**Headline:** 'Two Injured as Bus Skids in Malekhu'.

**Lead (what/where/when):** A passenger bus skidded off the Prithvi Highway at Malekhu, Dhading, at 7 a.m. on Sunday, injuring two.

**Body:** police, eyewitness, cause (speed + wet road), rescue, hospital, traffic disruption, investigation promised.

**Rules:** past tense, third person, no opinions, most important facts first (inverted pyramid).
questions.knowledgeNote: Report = headline + lead (5W1H) + details + source quotes. Opinions disqualify it as news.

questions.question: Write a paragraph of about 150 words on 'Environmental Pollution'.
questions.solution:
Model paragraph:

Environmental pollution is the contamination of air, water, and soil by human activity. Vehicles and brick kilns choke Kathmandu's air; sewage and factory waste poison rivers like the Bagmati; plastic litters fields. The result is disease, dead rivers, and a warming climate. Yet solutions exist: public transport, waste segregation, and community clean-ups. Each citizen's small action — refusing plastic, planting trees — compounds into recovery. Protecting the environment is protecting ourselves.

**Checklist:** one topic sentence, unified supporting details, concluding line, linkers (yet, result, however).
questions.knowledgeNote: One paragraph = one idea fully developed. Unity + coherence + adequate development is the marking trio.

questions.question: Write a formal letter to the editor of a national daily about the unmanaged garbage in your city.
questions.solution:
Model structure:

Sender's address + date → 'The Editor, The Kathmandu Post, Kathmandu' → Subject: 'Unmanaged garbage in...' → Salutation 'Dear Sir/Madam,' → 3 paragraphs (problem with evidence, effects on health/tourism, concrete demands: regular collection, segregation, fines) → 'Yours faithfully,' + name.

Formal tone throughout: no contractions, no first-name familiarity.
questions.knowledgeNote: Formal vs informal: full block layout, subject line, respectful distance — format itself carries marks.

questions.question: What is précis writing? Write any four rules of a good précis.
questions.solution:
**Précis** is a concise summary — usually one-third the length — keeping all essential ideas in your own words.

Rules: (1) read fully, underline key points; (2) one-third length, single paragraph; (3) third person, past tense, own words; (4) no examples, illustrations, or personal opinions; (5) give it a suitable title.
questions.knowledgeNote: Copying sentences fails the exercise — a précis proves comprehension, not transcription.
